title: Joseph, Son of Jacob
lead: Joseph son of Jacob and Rachel (not Joseph of Nazareth, the husband of Mary): Jacob's favorite son, sold into Egypt by his brothers, who rose from slave and prisoner to ruler of Egypt and saved his family in a famine (Genesis 37–50). His sons Ephraim and Manasseh became two tribes, and "Joseph" later names the northern tribes. Jews call him "the righteous"; Christians have long seen him as a picture of Christ.

sections.b: After Genesis, Joseph is remembered as the one whose bones Moses carried out of Egypt (Exodus 13:19) and who was buried at Shechem (Joshua 24:32). Moses' blessing gives him a rich portion (Deuteronomy 33:13–17). Chronicles explains the outcome of Genesis 48–49: the birthright went to Joseph's sons, but leadership went to Judah (1 Chronicles 5:1–2). Psalm 78:67–68 puts the rivalry most sharply: God "rejected the tent of Joseph" and "chose the tribe of Judah." Other psalms recall Joseph as the man God sent ahead (Psalm 105:17–22) and use his name for the whole people (Psalm 80:1; 81:5). The prophets speak of "the house of Joseph" for the northern kingdom (Amos 5:6; Obadiah 18; Zechariah 10:6), hope for "the remnant of Joseph" (Amos 5:15), and foresee Joseph and Judah joined again as one stick (Ezekiel 37:16–19), with Joseph receiving two portions of the land (Ezekiel 47:13). In the New Testament, Stephen retells his story (Acts 7:9–16), John mentions the field Jacob gave him (John 4:5), Hebrews counts his instructions about his bones as faith (Hebrews 11:22), and Revelation lists a tribe of Joseph (Revelation 7:8).

sections.h: Joseph in later Jewish and Christian writing
sections.b: Philo of Alexandria's On Joseph (first century AD) presents him as the model statesman, and Josephus retells his life at length (Antiquities 2.9–200). The romance Joseph and Aseneth and the Testament of Joseph praise his chastity and forgiveness, and the rabbis call him Yosef ha-tsaddiq, "Joseph the righteous." The Talmud's figure of a Messiah son of Joseph, who dies before Messiah son of David reigns (Sukkah 52a), draws on his name (see the topic on the Messiah). Christian writers from Tertullian and Ambrose (On Joseph) read him as a type of Christ, and some noticed that Joseph of Nazareth, too, is guided by dreams and goes down to Egypt (Matthew 2:13–15). The Qur'an gives his story a whole chapter (Surah 12).
